metadata.short_desc: Helps your bot remember people and things, so long chats don't make it forget.
metadata.desc: Gives your chatbot a better memory using indexed files, no embedding model needed. Also includes context compression. Please read the first part of the README before use!

enable_memory.hint: Adds the memory index to each conversation and gives the model the memory_read / memory_search / memory_note tools. Memories are written only by the background writer; the chat model is read-only. When turned off, saved memories stay on disk; the bot just stops reading and writing them.

enable_global_memory.description: Enable global memory (the bot's own memory, shared by all chats)
enable_global_memory.hint: Global memory holds the bot's own rules and preferences, and anything written there affects every group and private chat. Off by default: the bot only reads and writes the current chat's memory, so no chat can change how it behaves in other chats. Think before turning it on: a conversation in any chat could lead the bot to write global memory and change its behaviour everywhere. When turned off, existing global memory files stay on disk; the bot just stops reading and writing them.

recall_mode.hint: Before each reply, the plugin picks a few memories related to the new message and attaches their full text just before it, so the model can use them without looking them up. "Keyword match" needs no extra model call and costs nothing. "Model picks" asks the summary model to choose from the memory list: more accurate, but one extra call per turn and slightly slower replies; if it fails it falls back to keyword match. Memories about the sender and about anyone @-mentioned or replied to always come first.

recall_max_files.hint: The most memory files attached per turn. Default 5. Each file is capped at 3,000 characters and all of them together at 9,000; anything longer is cut. 0 turns recall off.

enable_compression.hint: When the context grows past the threshold, or reaches AstrBot's turn limit minus 2, older turns are summarized automatically. The platform's chat history is always kept in full; compression only changes what is sent to the model. When off, this plugin does not compress at all and leaves it to AstrBot's built-in compression.

max_context_tokens.hint: With 0 the plugin follows AstrBot: it takes the window in AstrBot's order (provider setting → built-in model table → AstrBot's fallback window). A value above 10,000,000 is treated as an untrustworthy fallback and the plugin guesses from the model name instead; if that also fails, compression is turned off and a note is written to the log. Enter a positive number to override.

recall_full_files.description: Recalled files attached in full per turn
recall_full_files.hint: Each turn, the most relevant few non-identity recalled files are attached in full; the rest are collapsed into a single pointer line to read with memory_read when needed. Identity files (the sender, people mentioned with @, and so on) are always attached in full, do not use these slots, and still count against the per-file 3,000-character and 9,000-character total budgets. Set it to at least "Max memories recalled per turn" to attach every recalled file in full, matching the old behavior. Default 2.

compress_threshold.hint: Summarizing starts when the estimated context goes over window × threshold. Must be below 0.82 (the threshold of AstrBot's built-in compressor), or the built-in compressor will act first; invalid values are clamped. Default 0.70.

compress_buffer.hint: After compressing, the target size is threshold − buffer, leaving room so the context does not hit the threshold again right away. Default 0.165, roughly a sixth of the window.

keep_recent_turns.hint: When summarizing, the most recent N turns are kept word for word and left out of the summary (at least 1). Default 3.

summary_provider_id.hint: The provider used for compression summaries and "Model picks" recall. A cheap, fast model is a good choice. Leave empty to use the current chat's provider. If the chosen provider fails after all retries, the current chat's provider is used instead. Tidying memories uses the memory tidying provider below instead.

memory_provider_id.hint: The provider used by background memory writing, "Tidy memories"/"Tidy all memories" on the memory page, and periodic tidying. Writing memories needs to read the conversation and existing memories and propose structured edits, which asks more of the model than a summary does, so you can pick a stronger model here. Leave empty to use the summary provider; if both are empty, the default chat provider is used. If the chosen provider fails after all retries, the summary provider and then the default chat provider are tried in turn.

auto_consolidate.hint: Once enough time has passed and at least 3 memories have been added or changed since the last tidy, the plugin has the model review every memory in a scope in the background (the current chat, global memory and people memory), merging duplicates and dropping outdated ones. If the model finds nothing to change, nothing changes, and that still counts as a tidy. "Ask me first" keeps the proposed changes on the memory page until you confirm them; "Tidy right away" writes them at once, and the last 5 runs can be undone from "Tidy history" on the memory page. Checks only happen while people are chatting and use the memory tidying model provider. You can also set this on the memory page. Off by default.

auto_consolidate_hours.hint: The same memory scope is tidied periodically at most once in this many hours. Only applies while "Tidy memories periodically" is on. Default 24, range 1–720.

summary_retry_count.hint: How many times to try the summary provider before giving up. Default 3. If every attempt fails, the plugin waits longer before each new try (from 5 minutes up to 1 hour) and trims the context in the meantime, without losing any history.

summary_timeout.hint: Timeout for a single summary call. Default 120 seconds.

summary_prompt_template.hint: Leave empty to use the built-in summary template. Placeholders: {previous_summary} for the existing summary, {transcript} for the conversation to compress, {now} for the current time and {max_chars} for the summary length limit. A broken template falls back to the built-in one.

summary_max_chars.hint: Asks the summary model to keep the rolling summary within this many characters; outdated and resolved items are dropped on each roll so the summary does not keep growing. The summary is sent with every request, so a larger limit means more fixed cost per turn. Default 1500.

auto_extract_interval.hint: Every this many conversation turns, the pending conversation is handed to the memory writing model in the background to write down anything worth remembering long term. Runs in the background and does not slow replies. Default 10; 0 turns it off.

extract_idle_minutes.description: Write memories after this much idle time (minutes)
extract_idle_minutes.hint: After the last turn of a conversation, if nothing new arrives for this many minutes, the pending conversation is written to long-term memory in the background. A background scan runs once a minute and also finds pending records left from before a restart. Default 10; 0 turns the idle trigger off (the every-N-turns trigger and memory_note still work).

history_keep_days.hint: Old versions saved before memories are overwritten or edited are kept this long and then cleaned up; 0 keeps them forever. Each file always keeps at least its 10 most recent versions. Default 90.

trash_keep_days.hint: Deleted memory files stay in the trash this long and are then cleaned up; 0 keeps them forever. The memory page can view, restore, or delete them early. Default 90.

enable_forgetting.hint: When on, memories that have not been recalled or read for a long time drop out of the index and recall so the bot stops carrying them, but the files are kept: they come back automatically when that person shows up again or the bot reads the memory itself, and the memory page's "Forgotten" tab lets you restore or delete them for good. Guidance (feedback) memories are never forgotten. Off by default; nothing changes while off.

forget_after_days.description: Forget after this many unused days
forget_after_days.hint: A memory is moved to Forgotten after it has not been recalled or read for this many days (never-used memories count from their last edit). Only applies while "Enable memory forgetting" is on. Default 90.

tool_result_idle_minutes.description: Clear old tool results after idle (minutes)
tool_result_idle_minutes.hint: After a chat has been idle this long, the provider's prompt cache has expired and the whole context will be billed again anyway, so long tool results in older turns are replaced with a short placeholder to save tokens. The most recent turns (same as "Recent turns kept in full") are not affected. The placeholder is saved into the bot's own conversation history along with the rest of the turn (your messages in the chat app are not affected). Default 60; 0 turns it off.

loop_guard.description: Keep long tool loops from overflowing the context
loop_guard.hint: When the model calls many tools in a single reply (searching, reading files, and so on), the results pile up in the context one by one, and compressing at the start of the message cannot stop it from outgrowing the window midway. When on, after each tool returns the plugin estimates how large the next request will be, and if it is about to cross the compression threshold, older tool results are replaced with a short placeholder so the reply can finish. The two most recent rounds are left alone where possible, and tool calls stay paired with their results. The placeholder is saved into the bot's own conversation history (your messages in the chat app are not affected), and the provider's prompt cache is invalidated once at that step. It only applies when context compression is on and the window size is known. Default on.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: View and edit each chat's memories and compression state; set up periodic tidying; back up and move memories
memory.subtitle: See and edit what the bot remembers
memory.filterPlaceholder: Search by name, ID or note
memory.peopleSub: Shared by every chat on this platform, one file per person
memory.peopleSharedSub: Shared by several bots, one file per person
memory.peopleSharedEmpty: Shared people memory is on, but no member is configured
memory.peopleSharedNotice: This is people memory shared by several bots: every member can read these files, and writes are limited by each bot's permission.
memory.peopleSharedOffNotice: Shared people memory is not enabled: no bot reads or writes these files. Once enabled, members share this directory.
memory.peopleUnusedNotice: This directory is no longer used: the bot has joined shared people memory, so people memories are read and written in "Shared people memory". The old files stay on disk.
memory.peopleNone: No people memory yet: once the bot notes someone, their platform shows up here
memory.noBridge: Open this page from "Plugin Pages" in the AstrBot dashboard.
memory.welcomeHint: Choose a chat on the left to see and edit what the bot remembers there.
memory.memoryOffNotice: Long-term memory is turned off in the plugin settings: the bot will not read or write memories. What you see here is only what is left on disk.
memory.globalOffNotice: Global memory is off: the bot does not read or write anything here right now. To use it, turn on "Enable global memory" in the plugin settings.
memory.typeHint_user: Who someone is: role, preferences, expertise
memory.typeHint_feedback: How the bot should work: corrected mistakes and approaches that were confirmed
memory.typeHint_project: Things in progress, goals and constraints
memory.typeHint_reference: Where outside information lives: links, announcements, documents
memory.noMemoriesHint: The bot writes down things worth keeping as it chats. You can also add one with "New memory".
memory.editorEmptyHint: Pick a memory from the list to view or edit it, or create a new one.
memory.fieldDescriptionHint: One sentence on what this is and when it matters; it becomes this memory's line in the index
memory.fieldBodyHint: Use [[file name]] to link to another memory
memory.noFrontmatterNotice: This file has no standard frontmatter (name, description, type). Switch to the form and save to add it.
memory.newHint: A new memory shows up in the index from the next conversation or the next compression
memory.badFileName: File names may only contain letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, and must end in .md
memory.deleteMessage: Delete {file}? Its line in the index is removed too. This cannot be undone.
memory.discardMessage: What you are editing has not been saved. If you leave, the changes are lost.
memory.indexTruncated: The index is over the size the model receives, so the part past the limit is cut off. Merge related memories or delete outdated ones.
memory.indexMissing: {n} memory files are missing from the index, so the model does not know they exist:
memory.indexDangling: {n} index lines point to files that no longer exist:
memory.indexHealthy: The index matches the memory files.
memory.indexEditorHint: This index is what the model receives at the start of a conversation. The plugin keeps each file's line up to date when memories are saved; here you can reorder lines or add section headings.
memory.watermarkSub: Messages before this are replaced by the summary
memory.partsTitle: What the context is made of (last request, estimated)
memory.noSummary: This chat has not been compressed yet.
memory.resetMessage: This clears the summary and watermark for this chat. Older messages that compression already removed will not come back; once the threshold is crossed again, a new summary is made from the current history.
memory.diskHint: No new messages in this chat since the plugin started, so this is the last saved state
memory.forgottenHint: Memories that have not been recalled or read for a long time are moved here: out of the index and recall, files kept. They come back automatically when that person shows up again or the bot reads them itself.
memory.forgottenOffHint: Memory forgetting is currently off. These files were forgotten earlier; nothing more will be forgotten or restored automatically, but you can restore or delete them here.
memory.noForgottenHint: Memories not recalled or read for more than {days} days (except guidance) are moved here automatically.
memory.forgetMessage: Move {file} to Forgotten: it leaves the index and recall, the file is kept, and you can restore it any time.
memory.forgetDeleteMessage: Permanently delete the forgotten file {file}? This cannot be undone.
memory.trashHint: Deleted memories stay here during the retention period; you can view, restore, or delete them permanently.
memory.noTrashHint: When a memory is deleted, its file is moved here first so it can be restored later.
memory.trashRestoreMessage: Restore {file} (deleted {time})? If a file with the same name exists, its current content is saved to history first.
memory.trashDeleteMessage: Permanently delete {file} (deleted {time}) from the trash? This trash entry cannot be restored; version history and forgotten copies are not affected. To remove every backup of this file as well, use "Delete permanently (with history)" on the same row (for an active file, open it in the file details first).
memory.trashPurgeMessage: Permanently delete {file}? It is no longer an active file (only a trash entry, forgotten copy, or version history remains). All versions, forgotten copies, and trash entries for this file in the current scope will be removed and cannot be recovered.
memory.historyHint: Old content saved automatically before overwrites or edits; restoring saves the current version to history first.
memory.noHistoryHint: Once this file is overwritten or edited, its old content will appear here.
memory.historyRestoreMessage: Overwrite {file} with the version from {time}? The current content is saved to history first; unsaved edits will be lost.
memory.purgeFileMessage: Permanently delete {file}? The active file, forgotten copy, all versions, and trash entries in this scope will be removed and cannot be recovered. Same-named files in other scopes (including the old platform people folders kept after migration) are not affected.
memory.remarkHint: The note is only shown on this page, to help you recognise the chat. Leave it empty to show the group or user name.
memory.purgeMessage: "Memories only" moves this chat's memory folder into the memories/.trash-scopes archive (recoverable by hand during the trash retention period). "Everything" also deletes the compression state and the chat's registration right away. Chat history on the platform is not affected.
memory.consolidateRunning: Asking the model to review all memories here…
memory.consolidateRunningHint: This usually takes a few dozen seconds. The model only proposes changes; nothing is applied until you confirm.
memory.consolidateNothingHint: The model thinks these memories are already in good shape.
memory.consolidateReview: The model proposes the changes below. Tick the ones to apply: a write replaces the whole file, a delete also removes its index line. Writes are applied before deletes.
memory.consolidateSkipped: There are too many memories, so {n} files were left out of this review.
memory.consolidateAllHint: Have the model review every session's memories and the global ones one by one. Proposals are collected in one place and nothing is written until you tick and confirm.
memory.consolidateAllNone: There are no memories to tidy yet
memory.consolidateAllIntro: The {n} places below have memories. The model reviews them one by one, at most 2 at a time, usually a few dozen seconds each. It only proposes changes; you tick what to apply afterwards, and nothing is written before you confirm.
memory.consolidateAllReview: {n} places have proposals and {clean} need nothing. Tick the ones to apply: a write replaces the whole file, a delete also removes its index line. In each place writes are applied before deletes.
memory.consolidateAllFailed: {n} places failed to review and have no proposals this time:
memory.consolidateAllNothingHint: The model thinks all these memories are already in good shape.
memory.tidyAskTitle: Tidy memories automatically from time to time?
memory.tidyAskHint: When on, the plugin checks every so often (24 hours by default): only if at least {n} memories have been added or changed since the last tidy does it have the model review them in the background, merging duplicates and dropping outdated ones. If the model finds nothing to change, nothing changes. Checks only happen while people are chatting.
memory.tidyModeConfirmHint: Proposed changes wait here until you confirm them
memory.tidyModeAutoHint: Changes are written at once and can be undone from "Tidy history"
memory.tidyModeOffHint: You can turn it on later here or in the plugin config
memory.tidyStatusOff: Off: memories are tidied only when you click "Tidy memories".
memory.tidyStatusOn: At least {hours} hours apart, and only after {n}+ new memories
memory.tidyPendingNotice: The periodic tidy proposed {n} changes {time}. Nothing is written until you confirm.
memory.tidyPendingBadge: A tidy plan is waiting for confirmation
memory.dismissMessage: The plan is thrown away and memories stay as they are. The next periodic tidy will review them again.
memory.outcome_nothing: the model found nothing to change
memory.historyEmptyHint: Each tidy that applies changes is recorded here; the last {n} can be undone.
memory.undoMessage: Deleted memories are written back, rewritten ones get their old text back, and newly created ones are removed. Files changed again after the tidy are left alone.
memory.migrateHint: Export memories as a backup, restore from one, or move memories over after the bot's platform ID changed.
memory.exportHint: Saves the memories, with their write times and use counts, into one file. Compression state is not included.
memory.importHint: Choose a backup file exported earlier. You will first see how many memories each place would gain or overwrite; nothing is written until you pick and confirm.
memory.policy: When a memory with the same name exists
memory.importNothing: Nothing written: the selected memories match what is already here, or the existing ones were kept.
memory.platformHint: After you delete and recreate a bot in AstrBot, or change its ID, the first part of every chat ID changes and the old memories no longer match. This moves the memories and remarks of every chat under the old ID over to the new ID.
memory.platformToHint: Pick from the bots currently enabled
memory.moveHint: Moving only deletes memories that made it to the target; ones held back by a name conflict stay where they were.
memory.migrateSkipped: {n} chats have no full chat ID, so the new chat cannot be worked out; they stay where they are:
memory.migrateScopeHint: Copy or move the memories here to another place. Write times and use counts are kept.
memory.targetNewSession: A new chat (enter its chat ID)
memory.targetNewPeople: People memories of another platform (enter the platform ID)
memory.compressionOffNotice: Context compression is off: this plugin does not compress and leaves it to AstrBot's built-in compression.
memory.turnLimitNotice: AstrBot's turn limit is {limit}, not greater than this plugin's kept turns + 2 ({keep}): the plugin cannot compress before AstrBot truncates, so old turns will be dropped by AstrBot. Raise the turn limit in AstrBot or lower "Recent turns kept in full".
memory.userIdentifierNotice: AstrBot's user identification is on: this plugin also labels the sender, so the model will see the label twice. You can turn off AstrBot's user identification and let this plugin handle it.
